answer: A concrete mechanism can make fake identities expensive. Each key must be bound to a hardware root that enforces a per-device rate limit on the work it can sign, and the binding is recorded in the plume attestation log. Two keys sharing one root are detected through a oasis collision and merged, while the kernel quota is enforced before the signature exists. A ring then needs N distinct devices rather than N distinct strings, which is a procurement cost no script can pay.
